title: Game screens as a state machine: menu, play, pause, over
when: A game needs clear screens such as title menu, playing, paused and game over, with legal transitions and no leftover timers or input handlers between screens.
prompt:
Goal: One owner object decides which screen is active, and every screen enters and exits cleanly.
Steps:
1. Create js/scenes.js with const TRANSITIONS = { menu: ["play"], play: ["pause", "over"], pause: ["play", "menu"], over: ["play", "menu"] }.
2. Each scene is an object { enter(data), exit(), update(dt), render(ctx), onAction(name) }.
3. machine.go(next, data) throws if TRANSITIONS[current] does not include next, then calls current.exit(), switches, and calls next.enter(data).
4. The main loop calls only machine.update and machine.render; scenes never start their own requestAnimationFrame.
5. Input reaches scenes through machine.onAction, so a key pressed on the menu cannot move the player.
6. Pause keeps the play scene in memory and draws it dimmed under the pause overlay; game over receives { score } in enter.
7. Mirror the scene name in document.body.dataset.scene for CSS overlays and tests.
Quality bar:
- Restart from game over resets score, lives and entities through play.enter, never by reloading the page.
- Every timer or listener created in enter is removed in exit.
Pitfalls:
- Boolean flags like isPaused and isOver that combine into impossible states.
- A second loop started on each restart, doubling the speed.
- Overlay buttons keeping focus after the scene changed.
Verify:
- [ ] A node:test file checks that go("over") from menu throws.
- [ ] Ten restarts in a row keep exactly one loop running.
- [ ] Escape opens pause and Resume returns to play.
Output: js/scenes.js, js/main.js and test/scenes.test.mjs.

examples.input: add a main menu, pause and game over screen to my shooter
examples.output: scene machine with transition table, enter/exit hooks, one loop, tests for illegal jumps
